Public Comment: The public is encouraged to address City Council on any matter listed on the agenda or on any other
matter within its jurisdiction subject to the rules of decorum described in Section 2.08.020 of the Norwalk Municipal Code.
If you wish to address City Council, please complete the card that is provided at the rear entrance to Council Chambers
and hand the card to the Sergeant at Arms. City Council will hear public comment on items listed on the agenda during
discussion of the matter and prior to a vote. City Council will hear public comment on matters not listed on the agenda
during the Oral Communications period.

Pursuant to provisions of the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the agenda, or unless
certain emergency or special circumstances exist. The City Council may direct staff to investigate and/or schedule certain
matters for consideration at a future City Council meeting.

Please adhere to the following procedures when addressing the City Council:
   Comments should be limited to 3 minutes or less.
   Comments should be directed to the City Council as a whole and not directed to individual Councilmembers.

Americans with Disabilities Act: In compliance with the ADA, if you need special assistance to participate in a City
meeting or other services offered by this City, please contact the City Clerk’s department, (562) 929-5720. Assisted
listening devices are available at this meeting. Ask the City Clerk if you desire to use this device. Upon request, the agenda
and documents in the agenda packet can be made available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability.
Notification of at least 48 hours prior to the meeting or time when services are needed will assist the City staff in assuring
that reasonable arrangements can be made to provide accessibility to the meeting or service.

Note: Any writings and/or documents provided to a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda after it has been
posted will also be made available for public inspection.

Writings and/or documents are available for inspection in the City Clerk’s Department, City Hall, 12700 Norwalk Boulevard during
regular business hours, 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., Monday – Thursday and 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., every other Friday; telephone (562)

The invocation was delivered by Dr. George Bojorquez, New Creation Church; followed
by the flag salute, led by Lance Corporal Goodwin, Young Marines.

CLOSED SESSION REPORT

The City Attorney indicated there was no reportable action taken on the matters discussed
in closed session.

CITY COUNCIL COMMENTS

City Council thanked all staff in keeping the community safe during the recent storms.
Councilmember Perez urged residents to stay safe and contact the City to report any
issues. Councilmember Ramirez encouraged residents to inspect their property after
storms. Councilmember Valencia reported on her attendance at the Norwalk Lions Club
Pancake Breakfast and thanked all who participated to make it a success, and also
thanked Norwalk High School Choir for their performance during the event; she also
attended the Door of Hope Youth and Family Resource Center Fundraiser and thanked
Arnold Alvarez-Glasman, City Attorney, for his contribution. Mayor Rios encouraged
residents to utilize the Norwalk Connect App in order to report various issues such as
graffiti removal, lost items, and bulky item pickup.

SPECIAL PRESENTATIONS

City Council presented a proclamation declaring February as American Heart Month in
the City of Norwalk, accepted by Kat and Elijah Pannell, American Heart Association
Instructors from EmergenCPR.

CITY MANAGER COMMENTS

Ozzie Ramos, Director of Public Safety, provided a report regarding the Preferential
Parking Program. Councilmember Perez requested staff review new state law Assembly
Bill No. 413 regarding increasing buffer zones and visibility around crosswalks that may
affect parking requirements.

Videos were shown highlighting the YouTube Multi-lingual Caption Tutorial, and the “Bi-
Weekly Review.”

DIRECTOR’S REPORT

Mr. Ramos shared a video and provided a brief presentation on the Public Safety
Department.

SUBJECT:  RESOLUTION NO. 24-13 - APPROVING THE TERMINATION OF THE FRONT
  STREET PARTICIPATION AGREEMENT

Background:

On July 6, 2021, City Council approved the Heart of Norwalk Vision Plan, which envisions
opportunities for new economic development within Front Street, Firestone Boulevard, and San
Antonio Drive corridors. The properties exchanged are part of the Heart of Norwalk project area,
which includes the City-owned parcels measuring approximately 0.57 acres identified as
Assessor’s Parcel Numbers (APNs) 8056-015-901 and 8056-015-900 and located at 12124
Firestone Boulevard in the City of Norwalk, County of Los Angeles (“City Property”) and real
property currently owned by Firestone Lofts, LP (“Developer”) measuring approximately 0.65
acres identified as APNs 8056-015-014 and 8056-015-016 and located at 13400 San Antonio
Drive in the City of Norwalk, County of Los Angeles (“San Antonio Property”). City staff is
working with the Arroyo Group to prepare a Specific Plan and create regulations and standards
of how change can occur within the project area.

On February 7, 2023, City Council approved an Option Agreement for the exchange of real
property for City-owned APNs 8056-015-900 and 8056-015-901 (“City Property”) and granted
the exclusive right to exchange for real property APNs 8056-015-014 and 8056-015-016 (“San
Antonio Property”), subject to further approval by the City Council and compliance with the
California Government Code Sections 54220 et seq. (“Surplus Land Act”). On October 17, 2023,
City Council adopted Resolution No. 23-62 declaring the City-owned real property located at
12124 Firestone Boulevard exempt surplus land pursuant to Government Code Section
54221(F)(1)(C) and approving an Exchange Agreement and Joint Escrow Instructions.

The City and the predecessors in interest to the current owners of the properties in the Project
Area (as defined in the Participation Agreement) previously entered into: (a) an Agreement for
Participation in a Commercial Revitalization Project within the City of Norwalk, dated August 11,
 City Council  March 5, 2024

1986 (the “Participation Agreement”), and recorded in the Official Records of Los Angeles
County, California (the “Official Records”) on September 29, 1986, as Instrument No. 86-
1297875, to govern the rights, duties, and obligations related to the prior revitalization of the
Project Area, and (b) a related Reciprocal Easement & Maintenance Declaration, dated
August 11, 1986 (“Original Declaration”), and recorded in the Official Records on September 29,
1986, as Instrument No. 86-1297876, to govern the rights, duties, and obligations of the Owners
related to the prior development, construction, maintenance, and operation of portions of the
Project Area. In order to facilitate new revitalization of the Project Area, the action to terminate
the Participation Agreement is necessary. Furthermore, as part of the transactions under the
Exchange Agreement, the City, Lofts LP and the other current owners of the Project Area (Lofts
LP and the other owners are collectively referred to as the “Owners”) are entering into, and/or
will be subject to, an Amended and Restated Reciprocal Easement and Maintenance
Declaration (the “Declaration”) to govern the rights, duties and obligations of the City and the
Owners in connection with the proposed new revitalization of the Project Area consistent with
the Exchange Agreement and the future development, construction, maintenance and operation
of the Project Area. The Declaration replaced the Original Declaration and recognizes the
changed development conditions and requirements and new ownership structures of the
properties in the Project Area.

Environmental:

The proposed action is exempt from the requirements of the California Environmental Quality
Act (CEQA) in accordance with CEQA Guidelines Section 15061(b)(3) under common sense
exemption which provides that CEQA applies only to projects which have the potential for
causing a significant effect on the environment. Where it can be seen with certainty that there is
no possibility that the activity in question may have a significant effect on the environment, the
activity is not subject to CEQA. The termination of the Participation Agreement terminates an
existing agreement and does not authorize any specific development.

Fiscal Impact:

None at this time.

  WHEREAS, the City of Norwalk (“City”) is a municipal corporation, duly organized
under the constitution and laws of the State of California; and

  WHEREAS, on August 11, 1986, the City entered into a certain Agreement for

SUBJECT:  ADVISORY BODY APPOINTMENTS

Background:

With the exception of the Planning Commission (which is commensurate with the appointing
Councilmember’s term) and five members of the Art in Public Places Commission (which is
established in the Norwalk Municipal Code), Advisory Body terms are for two years following a
City election. Advisory Body terms are from January 1, of odd years to December 31, of even
years.

There are vacancies on several Advisory Bodies: Art in Public Places (4), Historical Heritage
(3), Public Safety (1), Senior Citizens (1), and the Youth Commission (all 15). The Youth
Commission does not have any members at this time. The age range for the Youth Commission
is between 13 to 18 years of age. Each City Councilmember has three appointments.

Two of the vacancies on the Art in Public Places Committee are appointed based on Norwalk
Municipal Code §15.44.060, and require consensus of the entire City Council. Those positions
are: one at-large Community Representative and one Outside Authority with Expertise in Art.

Fiscal Impact:

N/A

Citizens Advised:

Citizens are notified of Advisory Body vacancies through posting of vacancy notices and the
Advisory Body term list, both of which are posted on the City’s website and at City Hall.

Background:

The Planning Commission (PC) reviewed Precise Development Plan (PDP) No. 2023-02 and
Conditional Use Permit (CUP) No. 2023-05, at a duly noticed public hearing, on November 8,
2023, and adopted Resolution Nos. 23-33 and 23-34 to deny PDP No. 2023-02 and CUP No.
2023-05 with a 4-0 vote (with Chair Barragan absent). Findings for denial of the project include
incompatibility with surrounding uses and the vision for the area, detrimental to public welfare of
the community, and inconsistency with the General Plan for creating a positive image for Norwalk
and providing a variety of goods and services along the Firestone Corridor.

On November 22, 2023, Andrew Miliotis on behalf of the property owner, Casa de Normandie
South, LLC, submitted an appeal of the PC’s action (Attachment No. 3) stating the action taken
by the PC is inconsistent with the General Plan, Zoning Code, the Heart of Norwalk Vision Plan,
and the 6th Cycle Housing Element. Per Section 17.02.210.H (Appeal Procedure) of the Norwalk
Municipal Code (NMC), City Council has the authority to uphold, modify, or reverse the PC’s
decision. The appeal was previously scheduled before City Council for consideration and final
action on January 16, 2024. At the request of the appellant, the item was continued to February
6, 2024, and to March 5, 2024, for the appellant to gather additional information on the history
of the project and property.
 City Council  March 5, 2024

Discussion

In August 2023, the applicant submitted a request to demolish an existing commercial building
and construct a new 3,511 square foot automated carwash facility with self-service vacuums at
11642 Firestone Boulevard (“subject property”). The subject property has a General Plan land
use designation of General Commercial and zoning of General Commercial (C-3). It is located
on the south side of Firestone Boulevard and the terminus of Woods Avenue (also known as
Assessor’s Parcel Number “APN” 8048-007-002).

The 1.00-acre subject property is developed with a 10,040 square foot one-story, single tenant
commercial building and bounded by commercial uses to the east and west, multifamily
residential across Firestone Boulevard, and single family across the railroad to the south. The
proposed express car wash facility would operate daily between the hours of 7:00 a.m. and 9:00
p.m. The community shared feedback and concerns during a community meeting on August 29,
2023, and PC public hearing on November 8, 2023. Concerns were in opposition of the project,
including incompatibility of the use with the desired character of the City and the proliferation of
similar uses in close proximity of the site. As part of the project, a traffic and acoustical analysis
was submitted to demonstrate the project’s minimal impacts to traffic and compliance with the
City’s Noise Ordinance.

The appellant asserts that the project should be approved because it is in compliance with the
NMC, General Plan, Zoning Code, Heart of Norwalk Vision Plan, and 6th Cycle Housing
Element, and that no detrimental impacts to the health and well-being of the community would
result from the project.

Pursuant to Section 17.02.240.C and Section 17.02.210.A of the NMC, a PDP and CUP may be
granted if the proposed project is consistent with the character of the community, is not
detrimental to the public health, safety, and welfare, and does not adversely affect property
values. The General Plan has objectives and policies to establish and encourage enhancement
of a positive image for Norwalk and to provide local-serving commercial uses. Community
members have expressed opposition of carwashes as the continued expansion of them conflicts
with anticipated development for the Heart of Norwalk area and is not consistent with Norwalk’s
vision. Diverse, active commercial uses that serve local residents are preferred and will
complement existing and new housing per the Housing Element. The subject site is designated
as a Housing Element opportunity site with a capacity of 29 units, including 20 low income and
nine moderate income. The Housing Element was certified by the California Department of
Housing and Community Development (HCD) on November 21, 2023. The PC’s action to deny
PDP No. 2023-02 and CUP No. 2023-05 was based on information submitted and raised during
the public hearing including incompatibility of the use with the desired vision for the corridor,
being detrimental to public welfare, adding to the number of carwashes in the area, and conflicts
with attracting quality uses and encouraging responsible development for the community.

INTRODUCTION/BACKGROUND

The 1.0-acre project site has a General Plan designation of General Commercial and
zoning of General Commercial (C-3). The project site is located at the terminus of Woods
Avenue and the west side of Firestone Boulevard (also known as Assessor’s Parcel
Number (“APN”) 8048-007-002). Surrounding the project site are commercial uses to the
west and east, an apartment complex to the north (across Firestone Boulevard), and a
parking lot to the south. The subject site has remained vacant since 2019, when it was
used as a real estate office.

PROJECT DESCRIPTION

David A. Storer, on behalf of Quick Quack (Applicant), is requesting approval of PDP No.
2023-02 to demolish an existing one-story commercial building (15,451 sq. ft.) and
construct a new one-story 3,511 sq. ft. commercial building and associated
improvements, and CUP No. 2023-08 to permit an express carwash facility. The site
improvements include 11 parking spaces with vacuums for customers, 13 standard
parking spaces, and one (1) accessible parking space. The carwash facility will be
operated by Quick Quack, which is an express carwash company having approximately
200 stores in multiple states. The proposed hours of operation are from 7:00 a.m. to 9:00
p.m. daily with 18 to 20 employees.

The proposed commercial building is located at the center of the property. It is designed
to comply with minimum setbacks, building height, and architectural design standards.
New parking spaces are provided north of the building, closer to the street, for convenient
customer and employee access and to buffer sensitive uses from potential noise impacts.
Parking stalls with vacuums are provided south of the building for customer usage only.
Other site improvements include upgraded landscaping, bike racks, canopies over the
pay station and vacuums, and trash enclosure located southeast of the building. Signage
for the site is also proposed in compliance with NMC Section 17.03.140, which includes
channel letter wall signs and a monument sign at the north entrance of the site.

Parking and Site Circulation

The total required parking for the use is 14 spaces, which was calculated at one space
per 250 square feet. The project provides 25 spaces, which exceeds the requirement.
Two driveway access points along Firestone Boulevard serve the project site. Upon
entrance to the property, vehicles would proceed in a westerly direction as they approach
the license plate reader/pay station canopy. They would then move in an easterly
direction through the carwash tunnel. Upon exiting the carwash tunnel, vehicles could
park to use the self-serve vacuum stations south of the carwash building or exit the site.

A Traffic Impact Analysis was submitted to the City and analyzed for any significant
impacts. Based on the report, the proposed project was forecasted to generate 10 new
AM peak trips and 10 new PM peak trips during a typical weekday. The report concludes

that the project’s transportation impacts related to vehicle miles traveled and
intersectional operation are less than significant and no further analysis was required.

Conditional Use Permit

Based upon public feedback from the project’s community meeting, carwashes are
abundant and ubiquitous throughout the city and undesirable for the City’s image.
Currently, there are 10 carwashes existing in the city; four of which are within a two-mile
radius. The closest carwash to the site is Norwalk Goal Car Wash, which is located across
the street. Commercial uses desired by community members include restaurants, grocery
stores, retailers, and other small businesses. In order to promote commercial activity as
desired by the community, proposed uses are to be evaluated in consideration of existing
uses and compatible with future plans. Furthermore, General Plan objectives stipulate
that land uses should be coordinated with future planned transportation facilities and
infrastructure, provide for larger comprehensive developments along major arterials, and
establish a positive image for Norwalk. The project site is within the (future) Heart of
Norwalk Specific Plan, which is in development and based on the Heart of Norwalk Vision
Plan that was adopted by the City in July 2021. The Vision Plan identified the area
including the subject site as the Transit-Oriented Residential District and supporting multi-
story apartments, condominium development, and occasional local-serving ground floor
retail uses along Firestone Boulevard. The draft Housing Element also identifies the
subject site as a housing opportunity site. Therefore, the proposed carwash use conflicts
with the General Plan and the vision for the Heart of Norwalk. The project will not serve
the public convenience and welfare pursuant to NMC Section 17.02.210.M.

Public Notification

The applicant, Quick Quack, hosted a community meeting on August 29, 2023, at the
Norwalk Arts and Sports Complex. Ten members of the public attended the meeting.
Feedback shared were primarily negative and in opposition of the proposed use, citing
concerns with the high volume of existing carwashes, proximity to other carwashes, and
the City’s public image. Public hearing notices were published in the Norwalk Patriot and
posted at locations set forth in NMC Section 1.08.030 as well as mailed to 253 property
owners within 1,000 feet of the property on October 26, 2023. As of the writing of this
report, staff has received no public comments.

ENVIRONMENTAL ASSESSMENT

Pursuant to the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA), staff determined that this
project would not have a significant effect on the environment and could be listed as a
Section 15303 Categorical Exemption. Section 15303 (New Construction or Conversion
of Small Structures) consists of construction of limited numbers of new, small facilities or
 Norwalk Planning Commission  Page 5
Precise Development Plan No. 2023-02  November 8, 2023
Conditional Use Permit No. 2023-05

structures. The proposed project would involve the construction of a 3,511 sq. ft. car wash
building and associated site improvements.

SUMMARY

In consideration of the community’s comments received at the community meeting and
of the vision and goals of the City, staff recommends denial of the project as it is not
consistent with the General Plan nor serves the public convenience and welfare. The
subject site is identified as a housing opportunity site in the draft Housing Element and
the proposed use will not be compatible with existing uses and development anticipated
for the area within the Heart of Norwalk Specific Plan. Multiple carwashes exist within
close proximity of the subject site and adding the proposed carwash will not increase the
positive image of Norwalk. City efforts to provide a wide array of local amenities along
the Firestone Corridor and opportunities for housing will be deterred as a result of the
project.

  RESOLUTION NO. 23-34

  A RESOLUTION OF THE PLANNING COMMISSION OF THE CITY OF
  NORWALK, CALIFORNIA, DENYING CONDITIONAL USE PERMIT NO.
  2023-05

  WHEREAS, Conditional Use Permit (CUP) No. 2023-05 was submitted by David A. Storer,
on behalf of Quick Quack Car Wash (“Applicant”), for 11642 Firestone Boulevard (“Subject
Property”); also known as Assessor’s Parcel Number (“APN”) 8048-007-002, a request to permit
the operation of a carwash facility on a 1.0 acre site; and

  WHEREAS, Precise Development Plan (PDP) No. 2023-02 was filed in conjunction with
this request; and

  WHEREAS, Sections 17.04.105 (Drive-through and drive-up establishments) and
17.11.010 (Land use Matrix) of the Norwalk Municipal Code (“NMC”) require the review and
approval of a conditional use permit by the Planning Commission of the City of Norwalk ("Planning
Commission”) for a carwash facility; and

  WHEREAS, the purpose and intent of requiring a conditional use permit is to ensure that
compatibility is maintained between a conditional use on a specific site, and other existing and
future land uses on adjacent and surrounding properties; and

  WHEREAS, the Planning Commission conducted a duly noticed public hearing on
November 8, 2023, at which time oral and documentary evidence related to the application were
received.

  NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED AS FOLLOWS:

  Section 1. The foregoing recitals are true and correct and are hereby incorporated as
substantive findings in the Resolution.

  Section 2. The Planning Commission finds and determines that the degree of
compatibility required by the Zoning Ordinance will be hindered with respect to the use of the site
as a carwash facility, considering the high volume of existing car washes in the City. The carwash
use will not promote the creation of diverse commercial uses desired by the community.

  Section 3. The Planning Commission finds and determines that the proposed use will
be detrimental to the public welfare and adversely affect the future development of the
surrounding area. The proposed carwash facility will not have a positive impact on the surrounding
neighborhood. As a housing opportunity site identified in the draft Housing Element, the proposed
project will hinder the potential to provide much-needed housing for the community.

  Section 4. The Planning Commission further finds and determines that the proposed use
is not consistent with the policies and objectives of the Norwalk General Plan to distinguish
Firestone Boulevard as a significant commercial corridor providing a variety of goods and services
and encourage the maintenance and enhancement of areas for creation of a positive image for
Norwalk. The project would add to the abundance of existing carwashes and would be the fifth

 carwash within a two-mile radius.

  Section 5. The noise study and traffic impact analysis prepared for the development
demonstrates that the project will have minimal impacts on the surrounding neighborhood.
However, the project will not serve to promote alternative modes of transportation or encourage
walkability in the immediate and surrounding vicinity as described in the Heart of Norwalk Vision
Plan. It would undermine pedestrian connections and would instead promote vehicle-oriented
development.

  Section 6. The Planning Commission, therefore, does hereby deny Conditional Use
Permit No. 2023-05.
